description: The plot illustrates how three accuracy-related quantities vary as a function of “Initial Confidence,” showing Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy across a set of confidence bins. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately 0.81 to 0.99 with tick labels shown at irregular intervals (including 0.81, 0.82, 0.84, 0.85, and then continuing by about 0.01 up to 0.99). The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 with major ticks at 0.2 intervals. The Final Accuracy series is a blue solid line with circular markers and vertical error bars; it starts near 1.00 at 0.81, stays mostly between about 0.88 and 0.97 across the mid-range (e.g., around 0.90–0.96), and ends near 0.98 at 0.99, with small local rises and dips (e.g., a dip around the mid–high confidence region near 0.95–0.96). The Δ Accuracy series is an orange dashed line with diamond markers and vertical error bars; it begins around 0.45 at 0.81, generally declines with fluctuations (including a low point around 0.15 near 0.86 and another low around 0.15 near 0.89), continues downward through the higher-confidence bins, and ends near 0.05 at 0.99. The Initial Accuracy series is a green dash-dot line with square markers and vertical error bars; it starts around 0.55 at 0.81, varies upward and downward through the mid-range (including values around 0.60–0.75 across many bins), rises toward the right side (around 0.80+ near 0.98), and ends near 0.93–0.95 at 0.99.
